title: Hosted API partial-response fallback and triage
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Customer escalations during tenant surges surfaced a recurring pattern of short windows where the Hosted API returned 5xx/timeouts for a subset of requests. Triage shows two correlated failure modes: (1) head-node scheduling pressure leading to stalled RPCs to the runtime, and (2) model inference slowpath triggers (longer KV cache misses + large sequence lengths) that push per-request latency beyond caller timeouts and then generate cascaded retries. The combined effect amplifies request storms and increases 5xx surface area.

This ticket scopes a targeted mitigation that both reduces immediate customer-visible 5xx and creates a safer rollout path for a longer-term runtime scheduling fix. We will implement a "partial-response fallback" at the frontdoor and introduce a short-lived per-tenant soft-circuit that: (a) detects slow backend response patterns, (b) returns an explicit partial result or a structured degraded response for non-critical requests, and (c) short-circuits client-facing retries by returning clear idempotency guidance and an advisory header.

Workstreams: 
- Instrumentation: add per-path histograms for backend tail latency and KV miss ratio; a minor trace span to quantify scheduling queue occupancy.
- Soft-circuit logic: per-tenant sliding window that flips to "soft-degrade" when >X% requests enter runtime slowpath for Y seconds. Soft-degrade returns HTTP 200 + structured payload {degraded: true, reason: "runtime-slowpath"} or a truncated streaming prefix for streaming calls.
- Partial-response behavior: for text generation, if runtime exceeds T_partial (e.g., 750ms) but is still producing tokens, return current prefix + metadata and continue async completion in background (for eligible customers). For sync-only routes or safety-critical customers, fall back to a smaller model variant.
- Retry harmonization: update SDK guidance and gateway headers to signal that requests with the new advisory header must use backoff window Z; ensure we do not expose inconsistent idempotency tokens.
- Rollout & safety: staged rollout using tenant allowlist, feature flag, and automatic rollback on increased error-rate or degraded-quality alerts.

Business goals: reduce immediate customer 5xx counts by 40% in targeted windows, prevent retry amplification, and provide observability hooks for the runtime team to tune scheduling kernels without urgent customer downtime.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard: new per-tenant slowpath dashboard visible in Console; SLO view shows 40% reduction in 5xx during synthetic surge tests
Behavior: when soft-degrade active, callers receive HTTP 200 with structured degraded payload or a streaming prefix followed by completion metadata
SDK: advisory header documented in SDKs and client-compat tests added to the sdk-integration suite
Safety: no customer-visible data loss for write-like requests; idempotency semantics explicitly preserved
Rollback: feature-flagged rollout with automated rollback if 5xx or latency SLO breaches exceed threshold within 10 minutes
